faq.label: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.heading: Clear Answers Before You Commit.
faq.aside: Timelines, pricing, ownership, support, the questions clients ask most before kicking off.
faq.cta: Still Have a Question? Contact Us

items.question: How long does it take to build a website?
items.answer: A standard business website typically takes 2-4 weeks; custom platforms and applications take longer depending on complexity.

items.question: How much does a website cost?
items.answer: Pricing depends on scope and features. We provide a clear, written quote after understanding your needs, with no hidden fees.

items.question: Do you offer payment plans?
items.answer: Yes. Most projects are split into milestone-based payments (e.g. deposit, midpoint, delivery) to ease cash flow.

items.question: Can you work with clients outside your home region?
items.answer: Absolutely. We serve clients across Africa and internationally, remotely, with video calls and messaging for close collaboration.

items.question: Do you provide ongoing support after launch?
items.answer: Yes, every project can include a maintenance plan covering updates, backups, monitoring and technical support.

items.question: What if I don't have a logo or brand yet?
items.answer: No problem. our brand identity and logo design services can build your visual identity from scratch before or alongside your website.

items.question: Will my website work well on mobile phones?
items.answer: Yes. Every website we build is fully responsive and tested across common mobile devices.

items.question: Can you integrate mobile money payment options?
items.answer: Yes, we regularly integrate mobile money and other local payment methods alongside card and bank payment options.

items.question: Do you sign contracts and NDAs?
items.answer: Yes, every project begins with a written agreement covering scope, timeline, pricing and confidentiality.

items.question: What happens if I need changes after the project is delivered?
items.answer: Minor revisions are typically included post-launch; larger changes are scoped and quoted as a new phase or covered under a maintenance plan.

items.question: Do you build software from scratch or use templates?
items.answer: Both, depending on your needs and budget, we recommend the most cost-effective approach without compromising quality or ownership.

items.question: Who owns the final website or application?
items.answer: You do. Upon final payment, all source code, designs and credentials are transferred to your full ownership.

items.question: Can you help migrate my existing website or system?
items.answer: Yes, we handle migrations of existing websites, databases and systems with minimal downtime and careful data preservation.

items.question: Do you offer training for our internal team?
items.answer: Yes, we provide hands-on training so your team can confidently manage content and day-to-day operations independently.

items.question: What industries do you have experience in?
items.answer: We've worked across healthcare, education, retail, finance, NGOs, government and more.

items.question: How do I start a project with VousTech?
items.answer: Simply request a free consultation through our contact form, we'll respond within one business day to discuss your needs.

items.question: Do you offer fixed-price or hourly billing?
items.answer: Both models are available; most clients prefer fixed-price quotes for predictability, while ongoing support can be hourly or retainer-based.

items.question: Can you redesign my outdated website?
items.answer: Yes, website redesigns are one of our most common projects, we preserve what works and modernize the rest.

items.question: Is my data safe with VousTech?
items.answer: Yes, we follow security best practices at every stage and never share client data with third parties.

items.question: Do you work with startups with limited budgets?
items.answer: Yes. we offer scoped MVP packages designed to help startups launch affordably and grow from a solid technical foundation.

items.question: What languages do you support for websites and apps?
items.answer: We are not bound to any language, we build and deliver in English, French, and any other language of your choice, based on what your audience needs.

posts.title: Why Mobile-First Design Matters for African Businesses
posts.excerpt: Most of your visitors will land on your site from a phone, often on an inconsistent connection. Here's what that means for how you should design.
body: For most businesses across Africa, mobile isn't a secondary experience. It's the primary one. The majority of visitors will reach your website from a smartphone, frequently over a mobile data connection that isn't always fast or stable.

That reality should shape design decisions from day one, not as an afterthought once the desktop version is finished. Mobile-first design means starting with the smallest screen and the slowest connection, then progressively enhancing the experience as more screen space and bandwidth become available.

In practice, this means lean pages that load quickly even on 3G, touch targets sized for fingers rather than cursors, and navigation that collapses sensibly into a drawer instead of a wide desktop menu bar.

It also means testing on real devices and real network conditions, not just a resized browser window on a fast office connection. A site that feels instant on a laptop can feel sluggish and frustrating on the device most of your customers are actually using.
The payoff is real: faster load times keep visitors from bouncing before your message even loads, and a smooth mobile experience builds the kind of trust that turns a visit into an enquiry.

posts.title: 5 Signs Your Website Needs a Security Audit
posts.excerpt: A website that looks fine on the surface can still carry real security risk. Here are five signals worth taking seriously.
body: A website can look perfectly fine to visitors while quietly carrying real security risk underneath. Here are five signs it's time for a proper audit.
1. It hasn't been updated in a long time. Outdated platforms, plugins and libraries are one of the most common ways sites get compromised.
2. You don't know who has admin access. If you can't list every account with access to your site, that's a gap worth closing.
3. There's no HTTPS, or certificates are managed manually and sometimes lapse. Modern hosting should handle this automatically.
4. Contact and login forms have no rate-limiting or spam protection, leaving them open to abuse.
5. Backups are irregular or untested. A backup you've never restored from is not a real safety net.
None of these issues are unusual, and none require starting over, but each one is worth addressing deliberately rather than hoping it never becomes a problem.

posts.title: Getting Started with Business Automation
posts.excerpt: You don't need an enterprise system to start automating. Here's how to find the first process worth automating in your business.
body: Business automation sounds like something only large companies do, but the best place to start is usually a small, repetitive task that already costs your team real time every week.

Start by listing the tasks your team repeats without much variation: sending the same follow-up email, copying data between two systems, generating the same report every Friday. These repetitive, rules-based tasks are the easiest and safest to automate first.
Next, map the exact steps of that one process before writing any code or choosing any tool. If you can't describe every step precisely, the process isn't ready to automate yet.
Then automate that single process end-to-end before moving to the next one. Small, working wins build the case (and the internal know-how) for tackling bigger automation projects later.
The goal isn't to automate everything at once. It's to free up a few real hours a week, prove the value, and build from there.
